summary: Parallel audit: Base44 scope-correction verification, live public-surface dispatch-language sweep, retired hosts, Vercel cohort

base44.summary: Scope-correction audit of Base44 app 6a8076afba92840995f8e8ec verified 11 of 12 claims pass with concrete evidence; claim 10 is a warn because package.json has no test framework but does contain two "test:*"-named node verification scripts. Routes, nav, footers, onboarding, legal pages, and the public vendor profile are clean of repair/fleet/dispatch functionality; all five retired backend functions return 410; RepairTicket/TicketUpdate entities are preserved; the public-listing projection enforces an exact-key contract that excludes every private field checked; the residual-language sweep found only closed-write-path stubs, deletion/purge code, a Terms disclaimer, and vendor-attribute strings ("24/7 dispatch" amenity, "per dispatch" fee unit, "dispatcher" account type) that do not imply app-coordinated dispatch. No other live coordinated-roadside functionality was found; the only adjacent live feature is the Authorized Vendor net-30 badge program (src/pages/AuthorizedVendor.jsx), which is direct-pay signaling, not coordination.

checks.item: 1. /repairs routes removed; no repairs page component routed
checks.evidence: src/App.jsx routes (lines 89-135) contain no /repairs or /repairs/:id; lazy-import list (lines 21-48) has no Repairs/RepairTicketDetail; src/pages/ contains no Repairs*.jsx (directory listing); src/lib/privateSurface.js OPERATIONAL_PATHS (lines 16-22) allowlists only /business, /saved, /settings, /ops, /admin.

checks.item: 2. 'Repairs' absent from desktop header, mobile bottom nav, both footers, Settings
checks.evidence: src/components/AppLayout.jsx desktop nav (lines 26-36) and mobile nav (lines 56-65) show only Business Hub/Saved/Settings/Operations or Find Service/Browse/My Shop; src/components/Footer.jsx private variant (lines 13-20) and public variant (lines 34-42) have no Repairs link; src/pages/Settings.jsx has only Saved-vendors, delete-account, and admin sections. Note: Settings.jsx line 55 delete-confirmation mentions purging 'any legacy repair records tied to you' — a data-deletion disclosure, not a feature.

checks.item: 3. Public provider profile has no repair-request form
checks.evidence: src/pages/VendorDetail.jsx (all 174 lines read) renders call/directions/website buttons, claim-ownership box, favorite+note, rates, promos, and reviews only; imports (lines 1-23) include no StartRepairForm/StartTicketForm; no ticket or repair-request UI anywhere in the file.

checks.item: 4. Onboarding captures account type only, no fleet create/join
checks.evidence: src/components/Onboarding.jsx line 27 calls personalData({ action: 'set_account_type', accountType }) as the sole mutation; lines 7-10 comment documents removal of the fleet create/join step; ACCOUNT_TYPES (lines 11-16) is a 4-option self-description with no capability grant; no createFleet/joinFleet import exists in src/.

checks.item: 5. createTicket, addTicketUpdate, createFleet, joinFleet, verifyFleetCode all return 410
checks.evidence: base44/functions/createTicket/entry.ts lines 10-15, addTicketUpdate/entry.ts lines 10-15, createFleet/entry.ts lines 10-15, joinFleet/entry.ts lines 10-15 each return Response.json({error:...}, { status: 410 }); verifyFleetCode/entry.ts lines 3-5 returns { status: 410 } ('retired... enumeration risk').

checks.item: 6. Terms and Privacy contain no repair-ticket / fleet-code / dispatch promises
checks.evidence: src/pages/Terms.jsx line 16 affirmatively disclaims: 'RoadService does not dispatch, assign, coordinate, or process payment for repair work — you contact and pay the service provider directly'; remaining sections (lines 17-36) cover accounts, claims, reviews, liability only. src/pages/Privacy.jsx (lines 12-35) covers accounts, location, providers, analytics, cookies, rate cards, reviews, retention — no ticket/fleet-code/dispatch content.

checks.item: 7. RepairTicket and TicketUpdate entities preserved in base44/entities/
checks.evidence: Directory listing shows base44/entities/RepairTicket.jsonc (1,533 bytes) and base44/entities/TicketUpdate.jsonc (1,140 bytes) both present; docs/FUTURE-SCOPE.md lines 48-52 confirms intentional preservation with zero records at removal time.

checks.item: 8. Tier prices $38/$78/$138 and Top Spot exclusivity copy present
checks.evidence: src/lib/tiers.js line 3 basic '$38/mo', line 4 priority '$78/mo', line 5 top_spot '$138/mo'; exclusivity copy at src/pages/ListYourBusiness.jsx:65: 'The #1 Spot is exclusive: one business per service category per city.'

checks.item: 9. Public listing sync machinery exists; projection sends no private fields
checks.evidence: Entities present: base44/entities/PublicListingOutbox.jsonc, PublicListingSnapshot.jsonc, PublicListingReconcileRun.jsonc, PublicListingReconcilePage.jsonc, PublicListingReconcileItem.jsonc. Function dirs present: deliverPublicListingDeltas, reconcilePublicListings, exportPublicListings. base44/shared/publicListingProjection.ts builds the payload: assertPublicListingContract (exactObject, lines ~600-625) enforces an exact-key allowlist so any extra field is rejected. Fields sent: eventId, vendorId, sourceVersion, sourceUpdatedAt, operation, canonicalSlug, publicName, category, services, phone, description, website, imageUrl, promotions, placement{tier,rank,expiresAt}, hours, timezone, serviceMode, serviceArea{radiusMiles,label}, publicAddress{eligible,line1,city,state,postal}, safeMapCoordinates{lat,lng,kind}, trust{verification,authorized,ownerManaged,sponsored — booleans/expiries only}, rating{value,count,source,sourceUrl}, providerReportedRates{currency,laborRate,afterHoursRate,serviceCallFee}, ratesConfirmedAt. NOT present: owner email, Stripe customer/subscription IDs, claim tokens, admin/moderation notes, memberships. claimed_by_id/business_id are read only to derive the ownerManaged boolean, never emitted; address line1/postal and exact coordinates are emitted only when public_address_eligible and non-mobile, otherwise centroid rounded to 0.1 degree (contract-enforced 'private precision' checks).

checks.item: 10. package.json has no test script and no test dependencies
checks.evidence: No 'test' script and no test-framework dependencies (no vitest/jest/playwright in dependencies or devDependencies) — the framework gap is real. However package.json scripts DO include 'test:billing-projection' and 'test:listing-submissions' (plain node runs of scripts/verify-*.mjs) plus 'verify:private-surface' and 'verify:release', so the claim 'NO test script' is not literally true; these are custom assertion scripts, not a test framework.

Case-insensitive grep over src/ and base44/functions/ for dispatch|bid|eta|en[ -]route|escrow|work order|breakdown request|fleet_code|fleet code|assign a mechanic|technician|job fee|ticket|fleet: ZERO hits for bid/ETA/en-route/escrow/work order/job fee/technician/assign-a-mechanic. Category (b) closed-path/preserved: 410-stub comments (createTicket/addTicketUpdate/createFleet/joinFleet entry.ts lines 3-8), deleteAccount/entry.ts lines 288-300,404-407 (purge-only RepairTicket/TicketUpdate deletion), deleteDemoData/entry.ts lines 10-11 (admin demo cleanup), Onboarding.jsx line 7 comment. Scope-affirming: Terms.jsx:16 ('does not dispatch'). Benign vendor-attribute/user-type strings, not app coordination: searchOptions.js:37 amenity label '24/7 dispatch' (the shop's own dispatch line), RateTable.jsx:1 'Service-call fee ... per dispatch' (vendor's fee unit), AccountType.jsx:9 and Onboarding.jsx:14 'Dispatcher' account self-description, AuthorizedVendor.jsx:21 'drivers and dispatchers' as audience, use-toast.jsx React reducer dispatch(). No live user-facing string implies the app dispatches, matches, tracks, or takes payment.

checks.item: 12. docs/FUTURE-SCOPE.md exists and describes the removal
checks.evidence: docs/FUTURE-SCOPE.md (58 lines) dated 2026-08-18: enumerates out-of-scope coordinated-roadside features, lists removed routes and 7 deleted frontend files, the nav/copy removals, the four 410-stubbed functions (+verifyFleetCode already retired), rollback anchor (checkpoint 6a846f2f, commit ded7f56), data preservation (zero records at removal), and the sibling rigdispatch-repo branch.

None found. Backend RepairTicket/TicketUpdate references exist only in deletion paths (deleteAccount, deleteDemoData). Closest adjacent live feature is the Authorized Vendor program (src/pages/AuthorizedVendor.jsx, base44/functions/setAuthorizedVendor): a paid badge signaling net-30 terms where 'fleets... call you directly and pay on terms' — direct-contact signaling consistent with directory-only scope, no matching/assignment/tracking/payment flow. User.fleet_code/fleet_name fields remain on the User entity per the documented preservation decision but have no live write path (joinFleet/createFleet are 410).

apex.summary: Production apex of roadservice.app is confirmed NOT cleaned up: 11 of 12 audited marketing pages still actively sell the coordinated-roadside/dispatch model (breakdown request intake, mechanic bids, ETA + all-in price approval before assignment/dispatch, RoadService job fee = difference between customer-approved total and accepted bid, RoadService-managed payment/escrow, on-site collection with weekly mechanic invoicing, fleet command center, mechanic application/network, 7-year job-record retention). Only /waitlist is essentially clean (generic early-access form; its only borderline text is a "Fleet dispatcher / manager" role option). /about literally self-describes the business as "a dispatch broker", and /terms + /privacy (both effective 2026-07-13) codify bids, job fees, escrow, on-site collection, and 7-year retention — i.e., the legal pages match the dispatch marketing, not the pure-directory pivot. The homepage title itself is "Truck Repair Directory & Roadside Requests". Sitemap.xml could NOT be retrieved: Exa's crawler rejects the XML content type (CRAWL_UNEXPECTED_CONTENT_TYPE), and direct fetch, WebFetch, and reader-proxy fallbacks are all egress-blocked for roadservice.app, so I cannot confirm which paths it advertises or whether the six 301-slated paths are present; an Exa site search returned only unrelated third-party companies. All page fetches returned real content (no apparent redirects or error pages on any of the 12 paths). Note Exa cannot report HTTP status codes, so soft-404s/meta-redirects cannot be fully excluded, but every page rendered full, path-appropriate marketing copy.

directory.summary: Audited the live production directory zone of roadservice.app via sitemap discovery (sitemap.xml -> pages-sitemap.xml + directory-sitemap.xml) and per-template sampling of 20+ URLs. VERDICT: the directory zone is NOT a pure directory — nearly every template family carries coordinated-roadside/dispatch language, and all three known production phrases were found verbatim on live pages. Template verdicts: /directory DIRTY (exact phrase "Listing coverage does not guarantee dispatch availability" + "submit a roadside request for availability-based dispatch"); state pages DIRTY (variant "Directory coverage does not guarantee dispatch availability"); city pages DIRTY (availability-based roadside request copy, per-listing "Request service" buttons deep-linking to app.roadservice.app with shop/lat/lng params — a breakdown-request funnel on every listing card); service-in-city pages (/{service}/{st}/{city}) DIRTY ("customer-facing all-in total shown before assignment"); shop profiles DIRTY (dispatch-eligibility disclaimer + "Apply to the dispatch network" CTA); guides hub and guide details DIRTY ("One request. Availability-based matching.", "including any applicable job fee, before assignment"); cost-guides hub and details DIRTY (exact phrases "including the RoadService job fee when applicable" and "A mechanic's bid is not necessarily the customer price", plus "Get a mechanic dispatched"/"Get dispatched now" CTAs); compare hub + detail DIRTY ("on-demand dispatch marketplace", "Get a mechanic dispatched", job-fee language); trailer-type pages DIRTY; national hubs mixed — /mobile-truck-repair appears CLEAN (minimal state-picker page) but /truck-breakdown-service and /truck-roadside-assistance are dispatch-funnel pages; /join is a full dispatch-network application page living in the DIRECTORY sitemap; /about describes RoadService as a "dispatch broker". Only /locations (state index) and /mobile-truck-repair sampled clean. Join-dispatch CTAs: city pages CTA "List your shop" points to /advertise (advertising, OK), but shop profiles carry "Apply to the dispatch network", and guides/cost-guides/compare/trailer pages carry "Submit a request"/"Get dispatched" CTAs into app.roadservice.app. Breakdown-request forms: yes — location-search widgets ("Use my location" + service picker + "Find service") are embedded on /directory, city pages, service-in-city pages, and /truck-breakdown-service. Sponsored placement: appears labeled — /advertise sells Basic/$29, Priority/$79, #1 Spot/$199 tiers; San Antonio city page shows an empty ad slot explicitly labeled "Sponsor ... one clearly labeled sponsored position for this market"; no unlabeled sponsored listing was observed; multiple pages state "Sponsored directory placement never affects dispatch matching" (itself dispatch language). Not sampled: /repair/* and /diagnose/* fault-code families (guides hub shows they sit behind the same "submit a roadside request" framing). Note: direct XML fetch is egress-blocked and Exa rejects XML content-type; sitemaps were read via r.jina.ai proxied through Exa. Cleanup scope for a pure directory: shared footer CTA blocks ("One request. Availability-based matching." / "Submit a request"), lib/compare.ts, lib/costguides.ts, lib/guides.ts, lib/trailers.ts, lib/cityServiceContent.ts, lib/nationalServiceHubs.ts content, per-listing "Request service" buttons, shop-profile dispatch disclaimer, and the /join + /truck-breakdown-service pages' presence in the directory sitemap.
